captions: Part four. The agent loop.
The small piece of code that ties everything
together.
Here is the loop at the center of
it all.
Step one, build context.
Step two, call the model. It plans and
picks tools.
Step three, run tools, with validated arguments.
Step four, observe. Results are clipped, and every
number goes into an evidence log. Then loop
back, until the model stops asking for tools.
Step five, verify the draft.
Step six, answer, with citations.
Step seven, remember anything worth keeping.
Watch the trace on the right. Every step
is logged, which is how you debug it
later.
Step one deserves a closer look. The context
builder decides what the model sees.
First, a stable prefix. Role, rules, the catalog
summary, and the metric glossary. It barely changes,
so prompt caching makes it cheap.
Then recalled memories, the ones relevant to this
question.
Then the conversation.
Then the question itself, with entities already resolved.
Last quarter becomes Q2 FY26.
Then tool results, clipped.
When the window fills up, older turns are
compacted into a summary. The numbers stay safe
in the evidence log.
In code, the loop is surprisingly small.
Build the context. Then, within a step budget,
call the model with the tool schemas.
If the model didn't ask for a tool,
it has a draft answer. Run the verifier.
If it passes, we're done. If not, the
problems go back to the model as a
message, and it tries again.
If it did ask for tools, run each
one, add its provenance to the evidence, and
feed back a clipped result.
At the end, remember what's worth learning, and
attach citations.
Let's run the example end to end.
The user asks our question.
The harness recalls two memories. The user prefers
crore, and this balance sheet file is in
lakh.
The model plans three sub-questions: the margin trend,
debt to equity, and why.
It calls get metrics for net margin, eight
quarters.
The result comes back as a small table,
with its source and unit. Every cell is
logged as evidence.
Second sub-question. The model calls get metrics for
debt to equity.
The conversion from lakh to crore already happened
at ingest, so the ratio is right. Debt
to equity falls from 0.35 to 0.25.
Third, the why. The model searches the earnings
call for margin drivers.
It gets back a quote, with the document
and page. That's all the evidence it needs.
Should you build five cooperating agents? Probably not
yet.
A 2026 paper titled Iteration Without Elaboration found
that a plain loop of think, run SQL,
observe, and fix is enough for text to
SQL.
Start with one agent and one loop.
Add sub-agents later, when your evals show you
need them. For example, one per company, in
a five-company comparison.
